title: ¿Y usted de dónde es?
desc: The same question as always, answered in a different order
setting: Somebody you have never met has sat down beside you at a lunch and asked the question everybody asks.

options.es: Vivo aquí, en el barrio de abajo. Vine de afuera hace cinco años.
options.en: I live here, in the barrio down the road. I came from abroad five years ago.
options.feedback: That order is the whole trick. Where you live first, where you came from second, and the conversation goes somewhere instead of stopping to look at you.

options.es: Yo soy de afuera, pero vivo aquí.
options.en: I am from abroad, but I live here.
options.feedback: The same two facts the other way round, and now the next four questions are about your country.
It sounds mysterious and it makes him work. He asked the first friendly question anybody asks in this country.

steps.speaker: Desconocido
steps.es: Ah, ¿del barrio de abajo? ¿Y por dónde vive exactamente?
steps.en: Ah, the barrio down the road? And whereabouts exactly do you live?

options.es: De la iglesia dos cuadras al lago y media abajo.
options.en: From the church two blocks towards the lake and half a block down.
options.feedback: Landmark, blocks, direction. Five years ago that sentence was a puzzle and now it comes out of you without thinking.
He will nod and he will not know where you live. The full address takes six words more.

options.en: I can send you a map.
options.feedback: Nobody sends a pin at a lunch table. He was placing you in the city, not trying to find your gate.

steps.speaker: Desconocido
steps.es: ¡Ideay! Yo tengo una hermana por ahí. ¿Conoce a los Espinoza?
steps.en: Ideay! I have a sister over there. Do you know the Espinoza family?

options.es: Espinoza es el apellido de mi suegra. Vaya a saber si son.
options.en: Espinoza is my mother-in-law's surname. Who knows if they are the same lot.
options.feedback: This is what surnames are for. Two people who have never met can place each other in about four moves, and you have just made yours.

options.en: No, I do not know them.
options.feedback: Probably true. Espinoza is also your mother-in-law's name, which was worth mentioning.

options.en: That is a very common surname, is it not?
options.feedback: It is, and that is not the game. He is trying to find the person you both know and you have just closed the search.

steps.speaker: Desconocido
steps.es: Puede ser, puede ser. ¿Y hace cuánto me dijo que vino?
steps.en: Could be, could be. And how long did you say you have been here?

options.es: Cinco años ya. Aunque a veces se siente que más.
options.en: Five years now. Though sometimes it feels like more.
options.feedback: Short and it opens a door without leaning on it. He has stopped asking about your country entirely, which is what the reordering was for.
Accurate. Half a sentence more and he would have had something to answer.

options.es: Cinco años, pero todavía me falta mucho.
options.en: Five years, but I still have a long way to go.
options.feedback: Modest, and it puts you back outside. He had already stopped treating you as a visitor.
